prerequisites: It is recommended to have previously studied Physics and Electrotechnics

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Ability to work, lead, and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling, and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.

syllabus_topics: Theory Block I: Signals and components. Types of signals. Basic components of electrical circuits. Basic theorems for circuit resolution.

Theory Block II: Semiconductors. Diodes. Bipolar transistors. Introduction. Definition of Semiconductor. Silicon Obtention. Silicon Crystals. Types of Flows in Semiconductors. Band Theory. Types of Semiconductors: Intrinsic and Extrinsic. The PN Junction: Forward Bias and Reverse Bias. Diode Concept. Diode V-I Curve. Electrical Characteristics of the Diode. V-I Curve Linearization with Ideal Diodes. Basic Circuits with Diodes. Other Characteristic Parameters of the Diode. Diode Datasheet. Other Diodes. Transistors. Transistor Biasing. The transistor in switching. Types of semiconductor-based components.

Theory Block III: Operational Amplifier. Concept of amplifier. Voltage amplifier model. Cascading of amplifiers. Differential Amplifier Concept. The Ideal Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp). Linear circuits using Operational Amplifiers. Linear circuits with Op-Amp. The real Op-Amp.

Theory Block IV: Digital Electronics. Digital signals vs. Analog signals. Information representation. Need and justification. Representation of NATURAL magnitudes. Representation of INTEGER magnitudes. Representation of REAL magnitudes. Binary codes. Boolean Algebra: definition. Theorems and properties. Logic Gates. Combinational functions: definition. Truth tables. Canonical Forms: definition. Definition of Minterm and Maxterm. First Canonical Form. Second Canonical Form. NAND Implementation. NOR Implementation. Functions with don't cares. Simplification of Logic Functions. Veitch-Karnaugh Maps (V-K). Simplification with V-K. Design of combinational circuits.

Practical Block I: Instrumentation. Learning to handle the instruments of a basic Electronics Laboratory station: multimeter, power supply, function generator, and oscilloscope. Measurement of phase shifts in voltages of an R-C circuit.

Practical Block II: Analog Electronics. Identification and electrical characterization of different types of diodes. Design, simulation, assembly, and measurement of half-wave and full-wave rectifiers. Design, simulation, assembly, and measurement of an inverting amplifier based on an operational amplifier. Design, assembly, and measurement of a non-inverting amplifier based on an operational amplifier. Experimental measurement of slew rate and bandwidth.

Practical Block III: Digital Electronics. Identification and verification of the operation of integrated circuits with logic gates. Design, simulation, assembly, and verification of truth tables for combinational functions from digital integrated circuits.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in in-person and/or virtual activities
Continuous evaluation of assignments, cases, or exercises (Digital twin practices)
Laboratory/field/ICT tools practices (written exam and/or oral test, review of practice reports)

assessment_rules: The grading system will be governed by RD 1125/2003 of September 5, which establishes the European credit system and the grading system in official university degrees. The final grade is composed of 5% for active participation, 45% for the theoretical concepts exam, 15% for continuous evaluation of 'digital twin' practices, and 35% for laboratory activities and their associated exam.
